sandhi.note: Visarga after a vowel other than a/ā, before a voiced sound, is sounded as r. It turns to visarga only at a pause or before an unvoiced consonant (खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः, 8.3.15).
ā + a → ā. The correlative सा and the demonstrative अस्मिन् fuse.
ā + ā → ā. The Gita Press marks the absorbed long ā with a double avagraha (ऽऽ), a printing convention: nothing is pronounced for it.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (prādi: the indeclinable सु ‘good’ as first member)
samasa.literal: in the good deed / good story
samasa.sense: this holy account of the Devī’s acts

morph.note: Passive present of √कृ: stem क्रिय- (कृ + yak, ṛ → ri before y) with the ātmanepada ending -ते. ‘Is made’: the satisfaction is produced in the Goddess.

The past participle used as a noun: ‘what has been heard’, i.e. the story once it is heard. The same participle stands just before in the locative absolute (सुचरिते श्रुते); the repetition श्रुते | श्रुतम् links the two halves.
Taddhita abstract (ṣyañ) from अरोग ‘free of disease’: अरोगस्य भावः, with vṛddhi of the first vowel (a → ā).
The present stem यच्छ- is a substitute: Pāṇini teaches यच्छ for दाण् ‘to give’ in the present system. With प्र it means ‘to hand over, bestow’.

mantras.anvaya: (… वत्सरेण या) प्रीतिः मे क्रियते, सा अस्मिन् सुचरिते सकृत् श्रुते (क्रियते)। श्रुतम् (एतत्) पापानि हरति, तथा आरोग्यं प्रयच्छति।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the relative sentence of 12.20–21: ‘the satisfaction (या प्रीतिः) that is produced in me by a year of offerings — that (सा) is produced when this story is heard once’; क्रियते is understood again with सा. The second line is a new sentence with श्रुतम् as subject and two verbs.
mantras.lit: (The) satisfaction (that) is produced in me (by a year of such offerings) — that (is produced) when this good story is heard once. Heard, it takes away sins and likewise grants health.
mantras.tr: The delight that a whole year of such worship gives me, a single hearing of this holy story gives me too. Heard, it takes away sins and grants health.
mantras.tr_note: ‘A whole year of such worship’ gathers the list of 12.20–21 (वत्सरेण, ‘over a year’) which the relative या there points to. ‘Gives me too’ renders the correlative सा with क्रियते understood.

comm.t: The Devī completes the comparison begun in 12.20: animal offerings, flowers, arghya, incense, perfume, lamps, the feeding of brāhmaṇas, homa, sprinklings, and gifts kept up for a year please her no more than one hearing (सकृत्) of this story. The second line adds two further fruits of hearing: sins removed, health granted.

The recitation tradition draws from verses like this its high estimate of the pāṭha itself: hearing or reciting the text is counted as worship in its own right, not as an accompaniment to ritual. The verse does not dismiss the offerings; it measures the hearing by them.
A modern reading: the verse sets a year of outward effort beside one moment of attentive listening and finds them equal. What it values is the attention, not the quantity.

words.en: the slaying of the wicked Daityas
words.g: n. nom. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); in apposition to चरितम्

sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra; the same in जन्मनां कीर्तनं and कीर्तनं मम.
Final t (voiced to d at word end) becomes the nasal n before the nasal m. The change is optional by rule; it is regular in practice.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (its first member दुष्टदैत्य is a karmadhāraya: दुष्टाः च ते दैत्याः च)
samasa.literal: the destruction of the wicked Daityas
samasa.sense: the battles of chapters 2–10, named by what they achieved
samasa.alt: Also readable as a bahuvrīhi qualifying चरितम्: दुष्टदैत्याः निबर्ह्यन्ते यस्मिन् तत्, ‘(the story) in which the wicked Daityas are destroyed’. The meaning is the same; the apposition is simpler.

morph.note: Genitive plural of the neuter an-stem जन्मन्: the n of the stem stays before -आम् (जन्म-न्-आम्). ‘Births’: the Goddess’s appearances, not births in the ordinary sense.
Action noun in -अन (ल्युट्) from the curādi root कॄत्, present कीर्तयति: ‘a telling, a proclaiming’.

mantras.anvaya: मम जन्मनां कीर्तनं भूतेभ्यः रक्षां करोति। युद्धेषु मे यत् दुष्टदैत्यनिबर्हणं चरितम्, (तस्मिन् श्रुते … 12.24)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is complete. The second opens a relative clause (यत् … चरितम्) whose main clause is 12.24a (तस्मिन् श्रुते …).
mantras.lit: The recital of my births makes protection from (evil) beings. My deed in battles, which (is) the destruction of the wicked Daityas —
mantras.tr: The telling of my births guards against evil spirits. And the story of my battles, in which the wicked Daityas were destroyed —
mantras.tr_note: भूत is rendered ‘evil spirits’ following 12.19 (रक्षोभूतपिशाचानां), where the same word stands among demons and ghouls.

comm.t: Two kinds of telling are distinguished: the recital of the Devī’s births (जन्मनाम्) and the story of her battles. Her births are the appearances told in the three caritas and the future ones she has just foretold in 11.41–55 (Vindhyavāsinī, Raktadantikā, Śatākṣī, Śākambharī, Durgā, Bhīmā, Bhrāmarī).
The tradition hears ‘births’ (जन्मन्) as manifestations: the Goddess is not born as beings are, which is why Medhas calls her eternal even as she ‘arises’ (1.64–66, and again in 12.36).

sandhi.note: Final n becomes the palatal ñ before ś, and the ś becomes ch. The grammarians reach the ch through an augment t inserted before ś (later dropped), since शश्छोऽटि applies after a stop; the spelling ञ्छ्र is the usual result.

Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra (also in वैरिकृतं भयं).

samasa.vigraha: ब्रह्मा (ब्राह्मणः) च असौ ऋषिः च, तैः
samasa.sense: the brahmarṣis, the highest class of seers
samasa.alt: Also analysed as a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, ब्रह्मणः ऋषिः, ‘a seer of the Veda (brahman)’; the compound is a fixed title either way.

morph.note: Genitive plural of the irregular stem पुंस् ‘man’ (nom. sg. पुमान्, instr. pl. पुम्भिः): the weak stem पुंस् before vowel endings.
√जन् in the divādi class takes the stem जाय- (ātmanepada): ‘is born, arises’.
Instrumental plural of the second-person pronoun: ‘by you’. The Devī is addressing the gods.

mantras.anvaya: तस्मिन् श्रुते पुंसां वैरिकृतं भयं न जायते। याः च स्तुतयः युष्माभिः (कृताः), याः च ब्रह्मर्षिभिः कृताः, (याः च ब्रह्मणा कृताः, ताः शुभां मतिं प्रयच्छन्ति — 12.25)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line answers the relative clause of 12.23 (यत् … तस्मिन्). The second opens a new relative sentence (याः च … याः च …) that continues into 12.25 and closes with ताः.
mantras.lit: When that is heard, fear caused by enemies does not arise for men. And the hymns which (were made) by you, and which were made by the brahmin seers —
mantras.tr: When it is heard, no fear of enemies arises in anyone. And the hymns that you have sung, and those composed by the great seers,

comm.t: The story of the battles frees its hearers from fear of enemies. The Devī then turns to the hymns: those of the gods she is speaking to (युष्माभिः — the hymns of chapters 4, 5 and 11), those of the brahmarṣis, and, in the next verse, Brahmā’s (the hymn of chapter 1). The text does not say which hymns of the brahmarṣis it means.

The verse is taken to include the hymns within the Saptaśatī among the things whose recitation the Devī herself commends, so that the stutis are recited as part of the pāṭha, not as optional additions.

samasa.alt: दाव alone can mean ‘forest fire’; then दावः च असौ अग्निः च, a karmadhāraya. Either way the compound means a wildfire.

morph.note: परिवारित is the past participle of the causative of परि + √वृ ‘to cover’ (वारयति): ‘made to be surrounded, encircled’.
Instrumental singular of the masculine an-stem ब्रह्मन् (Brahmā, the creator): the a of the stem is lost before the vowel ending (ब्रह्म-ण्-आ).

mantras.anvaya: (याः च) ब्रह्मणा कृताः, ताः तु शुभां मतिं प्रयच्छन्ति। अरण्ये प्रान्तरे वा अपि दावाग्निपरिवारितः (नरः … 12.29)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the relative sentence opened in 12.24 with its correlative ताः. The second line begins one long sentence, a list of perils in apposition to नरः, whose verb is मुच्येत in 12.29.
mantras.lit: and (those which were) made by Brahmā — they indeed grant an auspicious mind. In a forest, or even on a lonely road, surrounded by a forest fire,
mantras.tr: and the hymn of Brahmā — these grant a mind turned to the good. In a forest or on a lonely road, ringed by a forest fire,

comm.t: The fruit of the hymns is named precisely: not wealth or safety but शुभा मतिः, a good and auspicious understanding. The second line opens the list of dangers (12.25b–28) that ends with the promise of 12.29: whoever remembers the story in any of them is freed.

Brahmā’s hymn is the one of chapter 1 (the hymn that wakes Viṣṇu), which the Śākta tradition reveres in its own right. The perils that follow are the classical list of saṅkaṭas — fire, robbers, wild beasts, a king’s anger, the sea, battle and pain — for which the text is recited.

samasa.alt: Also वनस्य हस्तिनः (ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa); the sense is the same.

morph.note: Past participle of √ग्रह् with the connecting vowel i lengthened to ī (गृहीत, not गृहित), a special rule for this root; the root vowel ra becomes ṛ (samprasāraṇa).
Instrumental plural of the in-stem हस्तिन्: the n is lost before the consonant ending (हस्ति-भिः). The verb अनुयातः is understood from the compound before it.

mantras.anvaya: शून्ये दस्युभिः वा वृतः, शत्रुभिः गृहीतः वा अपि, सिंहव्याघ्रानुयातः वा, वने वनहस्तिभिः वा (अनुयातः) … (नरः — 12.29)
mantras.anvaya_en: Further participial phrases in apposition to नरः (12.29), each marked off by वा.
mantras.lit: or surrounded by robbers in a lonely place, or even seized by enemies, or pursued by lions and tigers, or in the forest by wild elephants,
mantras.tr: beset by robbers in some lonely place, or captured by enemies, hunted by lions and tigers, or by wild elephants in the forest,

comm.t: The list of perils continues with dangers from men (robbers, enemies) and from beasts (lions, tigers, wild elephants). The participle governing the elephants is carried over from the compound सिंहव्याघ्रानुयातः.
A modern reading: the dangers are those of a traveller far from help — the lonely place, the forest — exactly where no human protector can be summoned and only remembrance is left.
